the south stack: the halftone's tall stack at the crown's south end (x about 855 px), which T-3712 had reconstructed mid-depth; now triangulated with the Armour camera
the front's south end beyond the pavilion: lower, under a railed roof (x 880-1000, y 350-380 px), where the render carries the main mansard (as in the Armour photograph's record)

the pavilion's crown's top, dark and ragged against the sky (y 110-200 px): the crown's own deck now carries the K10 kit's iron cresting round its curb, its posts standing over the slates as the halftone's do, and the tall dark spike at x about 855 is the south stack, now 18.35 m: its top at y 117 against the halftone's about 105 (at the kit's 17.71 m it stood at about y 145), about 0.3 m short here where the Armour photograph reads it about 0.3 m over; the two readings disagree by about 0.6 m and the stack stands between them

the halftone is dark and coarse: window heads, the frieze, the cornice's consoles and every carved member read only as light and dark patches; the north stack stands about 30 px left of and 0.6 m under the halftone's (two cameras fitted on a resampled copy, pixel_aspect 1.195)

the halftone's principal storey reads as a pale arcade of piers between the lights (x 340-560, y 640-800 px): the lights' architraves and the pilaster strips between them at this screen; not read as a porch (the Armour photograph shows none)
colour: a newspaper halftone; and the picture is of 1928, twenty-four years after the scene (nothing it shows is read as an alteration)
